title: lore check reports a duplicate ADR ordinal as an ERROR naming both files (DEC-180 (1))
description: DEC-180 (1), accepted 2026-10-13 (opum-doc). Measured: `lore new adr` numbers from the working tree alone (nextAdrNumber, src/commands/new.ts:312), reading no ref, worktree or remote. Two branches that each create an ADR get different slugs (for example 0010-alpha.md and 0010-beta.md), so a duplicate ordinal merges SILENTLY with no conflict. `lore check` has no ADR-ordinal rule today (src/core/check.ts), so nothing catches it. Add an error-severity finding that groups docs/adr files by their leading numeric ordinal and reports an ERROR naming BOTH files when two share one. Compare ordinals NUMERICALLY (parse the ^(\d+)- prefix as an integer, as nextAdrNumber does), never lexicographically. The pair must make `lore check` exit 6. DEC-180 (1) also asks the message to name the repair command; that is part (2) `lore adr renumber`, which ships later — coordinate with team-lead before naming a command that does not yet exist, or word the hint without one. Prove both ways with predicted mutation arms.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A bundle with two ADRs sharing an ordinal (same leading number, different slugs, e.g. adr/0010-alpha.md and adr/0010-beta.md) makes `lore check` report an error-severity finding naming BOTH file paths, and the command exits 6.

Distinct ordinals pass: `lore check` reports no ordinal finding and exits 0 for a bundle whose ADRs are 0009-… and 0010-…, and again for 0099-… and 0100-… — the comparison is numeric (9!=10, 99!=100), not lexicographic.

Both directions are proved with a predicted mutation arm: mutating the check (lexicographic compare, or disabled) makes the same-ordinal fixture stop failing as predicted, while the distinct-ordinal fixture stays clean once restored; the mutation outcome is recorded alongside the green.
